newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes up $6.25 on heating oil, expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes up $6.25 on heating oil, expiry.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed sharply higher on Wednesday, buoyed by a strong rally on NYMEX heating oil and heavy buying on the front month ahead of next Tuesday's expiry, dealers said.
Nov gas oil closed up $6.25 a tonne at $214.75, with the Nov/Dec backwardation widening by $1.75 on the day to close at $6 a tonne.
"The spreads picked up and finished very strong in the last hour," said one IPE floor broker.
NYMEX heating oil, which traded up 1.68 cents at 67.10 cents a gallon by 1741 GMT, lent healthy support, said dealers.
A surprise draw on U.S. heating oil stocks reported by both the API and the EIA fuelled NYMEX heat's surge to a session high of 67.70 cents a gallon.
The EIA reported that U.S. distillate stocks fell last week by 500,00 barrels, while API figures showed a draw of 429,000 barrels. Analysts had expected a build in stocks of some 2.5 million barrels.
A squeeze on the IPE gas oil front month also appeared to be developing ahead of the contract's expiry on Nov 12.
Gas oil's performance helped take Dec Brent to a session high of $22.62 a barrel.
The contract dipped back to $22.49 at 1756 GMT, 30 cents up on the day.
The Dec/Jan spread was unchanged at +34 cents a barrel.
Some brokers anticipated a further retracement of gains ahead of the close.
"Both Brent and heating oil could tip off a bit tonight," a broker said.
